clue.text: Pay attention at commencement of stretching exercises

indicators.note: the commencement of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to sit up is to become alert and take notice
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fitness instructor tells the class to concentrate as the stretching routine begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are a familiar kind of floor exercise for strengthening the stomach muscles.

clue.text: Music of Australia boosted by No 1 from Sonny & Cher

indicators.note: number one from a word means its opening letter only
in a down clue, something boosted is lifted upwards, so its letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: opening letter of the name
the singer's name taken as written
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: An Australian song climbs the charts thanks to a hit by the duo Sonny & Cher.
explanation.walkthrough: The ampersand is just 'and': S from Sonny, then Cher in full, then OZ flipped upwards to give SCHERZO.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively, playful movement in a symphony or sonata, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: Take steps to leave after short function

indicators.note: one piece placed after the other means the second part follows the first in the answer

blocks.note: tan is the standard short form of the trigonometric function tangent
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone takes action to get away from a brief social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a party, but here it is the maths sense: tangent, shortened to tan.
explanation.definitionFit: To tango is literally to perform dance steps, a playful reading of the phrase about taking action.

clue.text: Amateur's out of form, under pressure in decisive match

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another is written below it, so it comes later

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
lay means non-professional; the 's is 'is', joining the parts
a player off their game is out of form

explanation.surface: A struggling amateur player cracks under the strain of a crucial game.
explanation.definitionFit: A play-off is an extra game played to settle a tie or decide who goes through.

clue.text: Section of Hull library, having withdrawn first part of Great Expectations, is gutted

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so the word is read backwards
the first part of a word here is just its opening letter
a gutted word has its insides removed, so only its outermost letters remain

blocks.note: lib. is the abbreviation for library, read backwards
opening letter of the word
first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A section of the library in Hull has lost the opening of a Dickens novel, leaving the staff devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the Yorkshire city but is the body of a ship. Great Expectations is a Dickens novel; its two words are treated separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilges are the lowest internal part of a ship's body, where foul water collects.

clue.text: Independent car maker is lacking employees, principally in Barking

indicators.note: the car maker's name is lacking the little word right before this, so those letters come out
principally means at the head, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for independent
Nissan is a Japanese car manufacturer
taken as written, then removed
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A news item about a car firm short of staff at its plant in Barking, east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but here it is the adjective 'mad', as in barking mad. Removing IS from NISSAN leaves NSAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking, short for barking mad, is British slang for completely crazy.

clue.text: Effects of sliding I'd reversed after signals changed

indicators.note: the signals are changed, so their letters are rearranged
the two letters are turned round to read the other way
one piece placed after another means it is written later in the answer

blocks.note: the fodder letters
the contraction written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone describes skidding about after the traffic lights changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissandi are musical slides from one pitch to another, so they are sliding effects in performance.

clue.text: One so lost in performance?

indicators.note: letters put in performance are acted out freely, so they appear in a new order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone so absorbed in playing that they forget everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a single performer, rapt in the music, made from 'One so lost' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist plays alone on stage and may well be wholly absorbed in the music they make.

clue.text: Shame to ban old clothing I exchanged for two shillings

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and the following item put in its place

blocks.note: embar is an old verb meaning to bar or prohibit
raiment is an archaic word for clothes
the letter to be taken out
s is the abbreviation for a shilling, so two of them

explanation.surface: A complaint that it is disgraceful to outlaw vintage clothes over a trifling sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in RAIMENT becomes SS, giving RASSMENT. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment is the awkward feeling of disgrace or mortification, close to shame in sense.

clue.text: Princess Grace's tip is to leave party showing a bit of leg

indicators.note: the tip of a name is its very end point, here taken as the opening letter
these letters are told to go away, so they are struck out of what follows

blocks.note: a shindig is a lively party
Princess Di, Diana, Princess of Wales
opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Princess Grace of Monaco slips away from a party in a dress revealing some leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Grace looks like one person, but the title and the name work separately. Princess Di is Diana, Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The shin is the front part of the lower leg, between knee and ankle.

clue.text: Outrageously bad lie about teacher is not unacceptable

indicators.note: behaving outrageously means going wild, so these letters are thrown into a new order
about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: the fodder letters
pupils address a female teacher as Miss

explanation.surface: A pupil's shocking fib about a teacher is judged to be acceptable after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissible means allowable or permitted, which is what a thing not unacceptable is.

clue.text: Hear Roy Orbison's contribution to US rock channel

indicators.note: a contribution is a share of the whole, so the answer is part of the run of letters

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An invitation to listen to Roy Orbison's part in an American rock music station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock channel' reads as a music radio station; it is a channel cut through rock. Roy Orbison was an American rock-and-roll singer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arroyo is a steep-sided gully cut by water in the dry American southwest.

clue.text: A number recalled uncontrollable movement of scepticism

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for the adjective

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a number is a song in a show or set
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A song brought back from memory conveys a restless, doubting mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' wants to be a numeral; it is a musical number, a song.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic attitude doubts that anything can be known about God, a kind of religious scepticism.

clue.text: Little woman, a Francomaniac?

indicators.note: a maniac is wild and out of control, so the letters before it are thrown about

blocks.note: Jo March is the heroine of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A small woman with a mad passion for France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Francomaniac' looks like one word, but splits into 'a Franco' plus its signal. The whole clue also describes the answer: a young woman fanatically devoted to France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maid of Orleans was a young peasant girl who fought with zealous devotion to drive the English out of France.

clue.text: Shop spy following information received

indicators.note: one piece following another is written after it in the answer

blocks.note: news is information that has come in
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: An informer betrays a spy once the tip-off arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' reads as the verb to inform on; it is a noun. A newsagent is a British corner shop selling papers, sweets and tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a newsagent's is a small retail outlet selling newspapers and magazines, and the trader's name stands for it.

clue.text: Fly in fast vehicle around North America

indicators.note: the vehicle goes around, so its letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: a GT, gran turismo, is a high-performance car
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Travelling around North America in a speedy car.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged insect, one of the many kinds of fly.

clue.text: Man and wife enthralled by God

indicators.note: someone enthralled by another is held captive inside their grip

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband and wife are both spellbound by a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is a chess man, a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is the lowliest piece on a chessboard, and chess pieces are called men.

clue.text: I'm looking forward to critic taking on Liberal

indicators.note: taking something on means taking it in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: a panner is one who pans, slating a show or book
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Someone eager for a reviewer to take up the Liberal cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person: a speaker who says 'I'm looking forward' describes themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A planner is someone who thinks ahead and arranges future events, so they are always anticipating.

clue.text: Songwriters: people making a fortune from lines about sentiment (chiefly)

indicators.note: about means around, so the first group wraps round the next piece
chiefly means at the head, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.clueFragment: people making a fortune from lines
blocks.note: palm readers tell fortunes from the lines on a hand
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sneer at commercial lyricists who get rich from sentimental words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a fortune' suggests getting rich, but means telling fortunes from lines on the palm.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalmists composed the psalms, sacred songs, so they are writers of songs.

clue.text: Union trouble over single issue

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the word reads in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
I is the Roman numeral one
issue means offspring, so a son

explanation.surface: A trade union stirs up a dispute over just one matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' and 'issue' suggest industrial relations; issue here means children.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a close link or relationship, sometimes a love affair, between people or groups.

clue.text: Firmly and correctly making fresh start

indicators.note: a fresh start means the opening letter is replaced with a new one

blocks.note: rightly means correctly

explanation.surface: Someone resolutely and properly begins again.
explanation.walkthrough: The R at the start of RIGHTLY is changed for a different letter; the definition tells you it must be T.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something tightly is to grip it securely and firmly.

clue.text: Naughty child's allowed outside, but he won't go

indicators.note: one word sits outside, so it wraps round the other

blocks.note: let means allowed
an imp is a mischievous child; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A mischievous kid is let out to play but refuses to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: a limpet clings stubbornly to its rock and will not go.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish proverbial for clinging, so a person who refuses to leave is called one.

clue.text: Model diagram/pattern in first place

indicators.note: the item in first place is its opening letter, and it also stands first in the answer
the slash is read as 'or', signalling the letters are another version of the word

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A specimen chart or template arranged at the very top.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is light: 'Model' as a verb means shape, and the slash marks an alternative form of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a standard example or exemplar that others copy, so a model.

clue.text: Claim member's consumed alcohol? On the contrary!

indicators.note: a thing consumed is swallowed inside something else
this swaps the roles just described, so the swallower and the swallowed trade places

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
a leg is a limb, or member; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: An accusation that a club member has been drinking, then a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary!' reverses the roles: the drink takes in the member, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, as when making a claim or accusation.

clue.text: Climbing across a ledge requires this rope

indicators.note: the answer stretches across the words, sitting inside the letters
in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: the tail of 'across' plus 'a' and the start of 'ledge'

explanation.surface: Mountaineering advice: getting over a rock shelf demands this particular line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across' is part of the hidden run as well as its signal: the letters come from acrOSS A Ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a long rope with a running noose, used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Wordplay for 'nuder' referring to basic clothing

blocks.note: the quoted word is the result; its letters rearranged spell the first part of the answer
the clue asks for a piece of wordplay, and this British slang word for rubbish is a standard signal to rearrange letters

explanation.surface: A setter explains how to clue a racy word while hinting at undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer itself as wordplay, with 'pants' as slang for 'rubbish', an anagram signal, so UNDER jumbled gives the quoted word.
explanation.definitionFit: Underpants are the most elementary layer of underwear, worn beneath everything else.

clue.text: Position of society, bereft of prime members, heading for extinction

indicators.note: the letters in prime-numbered places are the members taken away
the heading of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A society that has lost its leading figures is on the way to dying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime members' sounds like leading figures, but means letters 2, 3, 5 and 7, prime numbers: removing O, C, E and Y leaves SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or location where something is set, so a position.

clue.text: Turn soldiers back before French state is overthrown

indicators.note: turned back means read the other way round
a state overthrown is upended, so its letters are flipped round

blocks.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
état is French for state

explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the British army term for non-officers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to revolve or spin round an axis, so to turn.

clue.text: Superior sort of toy given to wayward son

indicators.note: a sort of thing is a version of it, so these letters take another form
something wayward strays from its course, so these letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters
the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A fancy plaything is handed to a badly behaved boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooty means haughty and condescending, behaving as though one is better than others.
